findings.summary: the three call-site guards asserted over SOURCE TEXT and were defeated by a comment: a '// was: healBrain() ...' line satisfied the kb_resume guard with the call removed, and a comment mentioning healBrain() satisfied the ordering guard with heal running AFTER the render. Replaced with behavioural tests that drive the real pi handler via a stub ExtensionAPI and the real resumePayload.
kb_resume had no working guard at all — one of the two faces issue #205 names was unproven at every level. Now routed through a shared resumePayload() and behaviourally tested.

silent restore: writeMeta() ran before the note was built and inside the outer catch, so a throw there (read-only mount, ENOSPC, EISDIR) swallowed the operator note while entries were already restored — the silent mutation heal.ts's own header forbids. Note is built first; writeMeta has its own catch.

the FAILS-OPEN test could not fail: it passed a nonexistent path, which early-returns at existsSync(wal) before the try block, so deleting the entire try/catch left it green. It now forces a throw inside the critical section.

healing ran PER TURN, not per session: pi's before_agent_start fires on every user message and the wal is gitignored (survives git switch), so healing re-appended entries committed only on another branch into the checked-out tree. Reproduced by the reviewer on the operator's real checkout (reverted). Now latched once per process, backed by a brain marker.

the L4's `said` predicate was not attributable to the injection: with --tools read the agent could answer from reading the restored file. Added the structural injectionCarries observable, which drives the real before_agent_start handler against a byte-copy of the arm.

`vfkb resume` — the verb CLAUDE.md tells operators to run at session start — never healed either; 'all three faces' was really the CLI hook, the pi extension and kb_resume. Now routed through resumePayload().

the governing docs still named the session-start hook literally (ADR-0064 §2, RFC-034 §2), which is how #205 was born. ADR-0069 amends ADR-0064 (immutable body); RFC-034 carries a dated amendment banner.

FIX-INTRODUCED: the guard moved down a level — resumePayload was well tested in isolation while NOTHING bound the two call sites the issue is about; reverting either to a bare renderResume was type-clean and left the suite green. Added test/heal-faces.test.ts, which spawns the real binaries (dist/cli.js resume; a real stdio kb_resume tools/call against dist/mcp-server.js).

FIX-INTRODUCED: the process latch did not bind the pi tier — pi-mcp-bridge is connect-per-call, so every kb_resume spawns a fresh mcp-server with a fresh latch, leaving the unbounded re-restore loop open on the very tier ADR-0069 exists for. Backed the latch with a brain marker.

engineSha described src/ while the scenario executes dist/ — and dist/ is gitignored, so checking out the pre-fix sha leaves the NEW build in place and a record could certify a baseline against an engine that never ran. Records now carry engineBuildHash over the executed bundles.

the RED baseline — the record whose central claim most needed provenance — had none, and the provenance fields had been added only to the GREEN record. It now states explicitly that it is hand-annotated and NOT self-observed, naming the exact indistinguishability, plus a predicateNote recording the RED/GREEN predicate subset relation.

FIX-INTRODUCED, SILENT DATA LOSS: healBrain called effectiveSessionId() with no argument, and that reads only $KB_SESSION_ID — while the Claude hook's real session id arrives on STDIN. The session-keyed branch was dead in production, so every face fell to a 15-minute wall clock and a brand-new session did NOT recover a brain destroyed by `git checkout --` (RFC-034 incident 1, unrecovered where the pre-fix engine recovered it). Reproduced three ways against the real binaries. The suite certified it because its only session-id test used the $KB_SESSION_ID override, a path production never takes. Fixed by threading the payload sid from the hook and scoping the wall clock to the single connect-per-call face; every other caller heals unconditionally.

residual of the same mechanism: kb_resume passes debounce unconditionally, so a hand-wired MCP-only consumer with NO SessionStart hook loses a recovery window (reproduced against the real stdio server). Not a wiring vfkb ships — `vfkb init` writes both the hook (init.ts:110) and the project .mcp.json (init.ts:223-236) — bounded to 15 minutes, and `vfkb resume` recovers on the spot. Filed as issue #259 (key the marker on parent pid) rather than held for a fifth round.

MERGE COMMIT: origin/main (f2ca756, ADR-0070) merged into the branch to clear a CONFLICTING state — main had moved onto the same files (review-gate.mjs, review.md, reviews/README.md, CLAUDE.md). A merge commit is never stripped by the gate (by design: a merge of unreviewed code must not pass on a parent's record), so this record is re-filed against it. The merge brought no code conflicts; both sides' machinery was verified TOGETHER on the merged tree: full suite 546/546 (the union of both PRs' tests), review-gate selftest 63/63, git-compound-guard selftest green both directions. main's side carries its own record (reviews/749631e...). No new review of the #205 diff was needed — it is byte-identical to the 4-round-reviewed 3970b25.
